Central Park soil moisture data

Source: R/data.R
cps_moisture.Rd

This is the Central Park Soil data used in Tree-Aggregated Predictive Modeling of Microbiome Data, with soil moisture as the response, aggregated to the family level. The soil samples were collected in New York City's Central Park by Ramirez et al. (2014). The counts were summed to the family level with aggregate_to_level(), as in the trac paper.

Usage

cps_moisture

Format

A named list:

y

Vector of n = 580 soil moisture values

x

Matrix of soil 16S rRNA amplicon data, with n = 580 rows corresponding to soil samples and p = 1492 columns corresponding to families

tree

Taxonomic tree of class phylo

tax

A data frame containing the taxonomic information for each family

A

A binary matrix encoding the tree structure with p = 1492 rows, corresponding to leaves, and 1634 columns, corresponding to all non-root nodes in the tree.

covariates

A data frame with the n = 580 soil samples as rows and five numeric soil properties from the original sample data: pH, total carbon (C), total nitrogen (N), their ratio (CN) and CO2_C. C, N and CN are missing for 29 samples.
